Midnight Office For Use at Home
Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us! Amen! Glory to Thee, O God, glory to Thee! O Heavenly King, Comforter, Spirit of Truth, who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: Come and abide in us, and cleanse us from every stain, and save our souls, O Good One! (From Pascha until Pentecost, “O Heavenly King” is not said;
from Pascha to its Leavetaking, “Christ is risen” is said three times in its place.) Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us! (3x) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. All-holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our transgressions. Holy One, look upon and heal our infirmities for Thy name’s sake. Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Amen. Lord, have mercy (12).
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Come, let us worship God our King Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God. Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ Himself, our King and our God.
Psalm 50
Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy, and according to the multitude of thy compassions, blot out my transgressions. Wash me yet more from my transgressions, and from my sin purify thou me. For I know my transgression, and my sin is continually before me. Against thee alone have I sinned, and have done evil before thee; that thou mightest be justified in thy words, and conquer when thou art judged.
Behold, in transgressions was I conceived, and in sin did my mother bear me. Behold, thou hast loved truth; the hidden and secret things of thy wisdom hast thou revealed unto me. Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; thou shalt wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. Thou shalt make me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice. Turn away thy face from my sins, and blot out my transgressions.
Create in me a clean heart, and renew a right spirit within me. Cast me not away from thy face, and take not thy Holy Spirit from me. Give me again the joy of thy salvation, and establish me with a princely spirit. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways, and the impious shall return unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation; my tongue shall rejoice in thy righteousness. O Lord, open thou my lips, and my mouth shall declare thy praise.
For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would have given it; with burnt-offerings thou wilt not be pleased. A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise. Do good, O Lord, in thy goodwill unto Zion; and let the walls of Jerusalem be built. Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifice of righteousness, oblations, and burnt- offerings; then shall they lay bullocks upon thine altar.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Here we may insert hymns from the Octoechos/Triodion
Then on weekdays, we may read the Seventeenth Kathisma (Psalm 118/119).
After the kathisma (if we read one), we say: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
The Creed
I believe in one God, the Father almighty, Maker of Heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord, Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Only-begotten, begotten of the Father before all ages; Light of Light, true God of true God; begotten, not made; of one essence with the Father; by whom all things were made. Who for us men and our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became man.
And was crucified also for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered and was buried; and the third day He rose again according to the Scriptures; and ascended into heaven and sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And He shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead; of His kingdom there shall be no end.
And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of life, who proceedeth from the Father, who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified, who spake by the prophets. In one holy, catholic, and apostolic Church; I confess one baptism for the forgiveness of sins; I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the age to come. Amen.
Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us! (3x) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. All-holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our transgressions. Holy One, look upon and heal our infirmities for Thy name’s sake. Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Amen.
Then these troparia in tone 8:
Behold, the Bridegroom cometh at midnight, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watchful, but again unworthy is he whom He shall find slothful. Beware, then, O my soul, let by sleep thou be weighed down, and be given over unto death and shut thyself out from the kingdom; but awake crying: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God; through the Theotokos, have mercy on us.
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
While meditating on that fearful day, O my soul, be watchful, kindling thy lamp, lighting it with oil, for thou knowest not when the voice shall come unto thee, saying: “Behold, the Bridegroom.” Beware then, O my soul, lest thou slumber and remain knocking without, like the five virgins
Both now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
We pray thee, O Virgin Theotokos, thou impregnable wall, bulwark of salvation, frustrate the counsel of the adversary, the sorrows of thy people change into joy, recall thy world and strengthen the pious; intercede for the peace of the world, O Theotokos, for thou art our hope. Lord, have mercy.
(40) O Thou, who at all times and at every hour, both in heaven and on earth, art worshipped and glorified, O Christ God, long-suffering, great in mercy and goodness of heart, who lovest the righteous and hast mercy on sinners, who callest all men to salvation through the tidings of good things to come: do Thou, the same Lord, receive also our prayers at this hour;
direct our lives in thy commandments, sanctify our souls, cleanse our bodies, direct our thoughts, cleanse our minds, and deliver us from every tribulation, wickedness, and affliction; encompass us by Thy holy angels, that guarded and guided by their host, we may attain to the unity of the faith, and to the understanding of Thine unapproachable glory, for blessed art thou uunto ages of ages. Amen. Lord, have mercy.
(3) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. More honorable than the Cherubim and more glorious without compare than the Seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word: verily, Theotokos, we magnify thee. Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ have mercy on us. Amen. During the Great Fast, (when the Alleluia is sung), the prayer of St. Ephrem of Syria is read now.
O Lord and Master of my life, the spirit of idleness, of despondency, of love of power, and of idle words, grant me not. (Prostration) But the spirit of continence, of humility, of patience, and of love, do Thou grant unto me Thy servant. (Prostration) Yea O Lord and King, grant unto me to perceive mine own offences and not to judge my brother; for blessed art Thou uunto ages of ages. Amen. (Prostration)
Then 12 bows to the waist while saying:
O God, cleanse Thou me a sinner and have mercy on me (12).
OR
O God, have mercy on me a sinner (3). O God, cleanse Thou me a sinner and have mercy on me (3). Thou hast created me, O Lord, have mercy on me (3). Countless times have I sinned, O Lord, forgive me. (3)
Then repeat the prayer in full, and conclude with a prostration.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
The prayer of St. Mardarius
O Master, God, Father Almighty, Lord, Only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit, one Godhead, one Power: have mercy on me a sinner, and, by the judgements which Thou discernest, save me Thine unworthy servant, for blessed art thou unto ages of ages. Amen.
A Prayer of St. Basil the Great
Almighty Lord, the God of hosts and of all flesh, who livest in the heights, yet lookest down on the humble, proving the hearts and emotions, clearly foreknowing the secrets of men: Thou art the Light without beginning, in Whom there is no variation nor shadow of change. O Immortal King, accept the prayers which we now offer Thee from defiled lips. Free us from the sins we have committed in deed, word or thought, knowingly and unknowingly.
Cleanse us from all defilement of flesh and spirit. Grant us to pass through the entire night of this present life with a watchful heart and a sober mind, awaiting the coming of the bright and manifest day of Thine only-begotten Son, our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, when the Judge of all will come with glory to reward each according to his deeds.
May we not be found fallen and lazy, but alert and roused to action, prepared to enter into His joy and the divine chamber of His glory, where the voice of those who feast is unceasing and indescribable is the delight of those who behold the inexpressible beauty of Thy countenance. For Thou art the true Light which enlightens and sanctifies all, and all creation hymns Thee uunto ages of ages. Amen
Another Prayer of St. Basil We bless Thee, most high God and Lord of mercies, Who ever doest great and unfathomable things for us – glorious and awesome things without number. Thou givest us sleep for the repose of our frailty, relieving the labors of our over-burdened flesh. We thank Thee for not destroying us in our lawlessness. Instead, Thou has shown Thy usual love for mankind, and raised us, as we lay in despair, to glorify Thy Reign.
Therefore, we implore Thy boundless goodness: enlighten our thoughts and eyes, and awaken our minds from the heavy sleep of laziness. Open our lips and fill them with Thy praise, that we may unwaveringly hymn and confess Thee, the God glorified in all and by all, Father without beginning, with Thine only-begotten Son and Thine all-holy, and life-giving Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
A Prayer of St. Eustratius
Greatly will I magnify thee, O Lord, for Thou didst look upon my humility and didst not shut me up in the hands of the enemy, but thou hast saved my soul from necessities. And now, O Master, let thy hand shelter me, and let thy mercy come upon me, for my soul is disquieted and pained at its departure from this my wretched and foul body.
May the evil counsel of the foe never meet and hinder it in the darkness because of the sins that in ignorance and with knowledge I have committed in this life. Be gracious unto me, O Mater, and let not my soul see the murky and dark vision of evil demons, but let it be received by thy radiant and shining angels. Give glory to thy holy name, and by thy power lead me to thy divine judgment seat.
When I shall be judged, let not the hand of the prince of this world take me in order to drag me, a sinner, down into the depths of hell, but stand thou near me, and be unto me a Savior and Helper. Let these bodily torments be a joy unto thy servants. Have mercy, O Lord, on my soul made foul with the passion s of this life, and receive it cleansed through repentance and confession, for blessed art thou uunto ages of ages. Amen.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Come, let us worship God our King. Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God. Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ Himself, our King and our God.
Psalm 120
I lifted up mine eyes unto the mountains, whence cometh my help. My help is from the Lord, who hath made heaven and earth. Let not my foot be given to wavering, nor He that keepeth thee slumber. Behold, He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. The Lord shall keep thee; the Lord is thy shield upon thy right hand. By day the sun shall not smite thee, nor the moon by night. The Lord shall keep thee from all evil; the Lord shall keep thy soul.
The Lord shall keep thy coming in and thy going out henceforth and forevermore.
Psalm 133
Behold now, bless the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord, that stand in the house of the Lord, n the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands in the sanctuaries and bless ye the Lord. May the Lord bless thee out of Zion, He that made heaven and earth.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now an ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us! (3x) Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. All-holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our transgressions. Holy One, look upon and heal our infirmities for Thy name’s sake. Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. Amen.
These Troparia for the Departed in Tone 2
O Lord, as thou art good, remember thy servants, and pardon them in whatsoever they have sinned during their life, for none is without sin, but thou who art able to give rest to the departed.
Out of the depth of wisdom and with love of man dost thou dispense all things, and dost distribute to all that which is expedient, O only Artificer; give rest, O Lord, to the souls of they servants, for they did put their hope in thee, our Maker and our Fashioner and our God.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit. With the saints give rest, O Christ, to the souls of Thy servant(s), where there is neither sickness nor sorrow, and no more sighing, but life everlasting.
Now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen. Theotokion
We bless thee in every generation, O Virgin Theotokos, for in thee the uncontained Christ was well-pleased to be contained. Blessed are we also that have thee as a Protectress, for day and night, thou dost intercede for us, and the scepters of kings by thy supplications are strengthened. Wherefore in hymning thee, we cry to thee: Rejoice, O thou who art full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
Lord, have mercy (12).
And these prayers:
The Remembrancer Remember, O Lord, our fathers and brethren who have fallen asleep in the hope of the resurrection unto life eternal, and all them that in piety and faith have completed their lives.
Pardon every sin committed by them in word or deed or thought, and settle them in a place of light, in a place of verdure, in a place of repose, whence all sickness, sorrow, and sighing have fled away, where the light of thy face watcheth over and gladdeneth all thy Saints from the ages. Grant them and us thy kingdom and participation in thine endless and blessed life.
For thou art the Resurrection, and the Life, and the Repose of thy servants who have fallen asleep, O Christ our God, and unto thee do we send up glory, together with thy Father, who is without beginning, and thine all-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, not and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
O most glorious ever-virgin Mother of Christ God, offer our prayers unto thy Son and our God, that He may, through thee, save our souls.
All my hope I place on thee, O Mother of God; keep me beneath thy shelter.
My hope is the Father, my refuge is the Son, my protection is the Holy Spirit; O Holy Trinity, glory to thee.
And these Troparia in tone 6:
Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, for laying aside all excuse, we sinners offer unto Thee as to our Master, this supplication: have mercy on us.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. O Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have put our hope. Do not be angry with us, neither remember our iniquities, but look down on us even now, since Thou art compassionate, and deliver us from our enemies; for Thou art our God and we are Thy people; we are all the works of Thy hands, and we call on Thy Name.
Midnight Office For Use at Home
Now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
O Blessed Theotokos, open the doors of compassion to us whose hope is in thee, that we may not perish but be delivered from adversities, through thee who art the salvation of the Christian people.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and uunto ages of ages. Amen.
Lord, have mercy (3). Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God have mercy on us. Amen.

Basil's Liturgy, as the latter, in turn, was a later and abbreviated form of a
 still earlier Liturgy.
 It is appointed to be used on the Sundays of the Great Fast (Lent), except
 on Palm Sunday; on Holy Thursday and Holy Saturday; and on Christmas
 Day and the Epiphany, when those feasts fall upon Sunday or Monday ; other-
 wise, on the days preceding those feasts. Also, on St. Basil's Day, January I;
 in all, ten times in the course of the year.
 The Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts, so called because the Holy Gifts
 which have previously been consecrated are used for the Holy Communion,
 has existed from ancient times, although, in its present form, it is ascribed to
 St. Gregory Homiliastes of Rome (sixth century). The Orthodox Church de-
 crees that this Liturgy shall be celebrated during the Great Fast (but at no
 other time), since the triumphantly joyous feelings associated with the corn-
 plete Liturgy and the consecration of the Holy Gifts are incompatible with
 the strictness of the Fast. Hence it is ordained that the complete Liturgy
 shall be celebrated only on Saturdays and Sundays during the weeks of the
 Great Fast (Lent). The customary days for the celebration of the Liturgy
 of the Presanctified Gifts are Wednesday and Friday of every week, and on
 Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week.
 The Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts consists of Vespers (and therefore is
THE DIVINE LITURGY 65
appointed for a late hour in the day), and of a portion of the ordinary Liturgy,
omitting the most essential part of the latter, namely, the consecration of the
Gifts. The Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts is usually preceded by the read-
ing of the Third, Sixth and Ninth Hours, and of the Typical Psalms. Under
certain circumstances an earlier celebration is admissible.
 The usual hour for celebrating the ordinary Liturgy is, not earlier than
dawn, and wt later than noon.
 For the celebration of the Mystery of the Eucharist the following are indis-
pensable : A Priest or a Bishop regularly ordained, and having a steadfast
will and intention to fulfil the Mystery of the Lord's Body and Blood. Of
material things : five Altar-breads, made of pure wheaten flour, and leavened ;
wine of the grape. The accomplishment of the Mystery through prayer and
words, with the blessing of the Priest's hand: "And make this bread the
precious Body of thy Christ, and also that which is in this cup the precious
 Blood of thy Christ, transmuting them by thy Holy Spirit."
 In addition to the above, the following things are indispensable for the
Liturgy : A Corporal (Antimfm),* consecrated by a Bishop ; vestments for
the Priest, consisting of a cassock (stikhdr), a stole (cpitraRhfI), gauntlets
(p6m/chz], girdle (pbynr), and chasuble w16n) ; vessels, -a chalice, a paten,
a star-cover, a spear, a spoon ; veils, a censer, a service book ; lights burning
on the altar ; and an acolyte.
 Only one Liturgy may be celebrated on any Altar in the course of one day ;
 and no Bishop or Priest may celebrate more than one Liturgy in the course
of one and the same day.
 The Priest who enters upon the celebration of the Liturgy must be free
from inhibition, and from mortal sin, and must prepare himself,- spiritually, ,
by reconciling himself with all men, by penitence, and the appointed devo-
tions ; bodily, by abstinence from food and drink(from midnight at the least),
and from fleshly desires, and'by cleanliness of body and garments.
 The appointed devotions consist of the celebration or the hearing of the
Evening and Morning Services and Prayers ; and there must also be read : .
On Monday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus, the Invocation to the Birthgiver
of God, the Canon to the Archangels; and, if he so desire, to his Guardian
Angel. On Tuesday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus, the Invocation to the
Birth-giver of God, to John the Forerunner, and to his Guardian Angel. On
Wednesday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus, the Canon to the Birth-giver of
God, and to his Guardian Angel. On Thursday: The Canon to the Lord
Jesus, the Invocation to the Birth-giver of God, to his Guardian Angel, to
the Holy Apostles ; and, if he so desire, to St. Nicholas. On Friday, the
Canon to the Life-giving Cross, the Invocation to the Birth-giver of God,
and to his Guardian Angel. On Saturday: The Canon to the Lord Jesus,
the Chant of Prayer and Praise (Akd@t) to the Birth-giver of God, to his
Guardian Angel, and to all the Saints. On Sunday : The Canon to the Lord
Jesus, the Invocation to the Birth-giver of God, and to his Guardian Angel.
 In addition to these, on every occasion, the Canon of the Communion, and
the Prayers before the Communion. (See I&.)

documents.search_text: the office of oblation complete office of oblation from the public-domain 1906 service book. basil's liturgy, as the latter, in turn, was a later and abbreviated form of a still earlier liturgy. it is appointed to be used on the sundays of the great fast (lent), except on palm sunday; on holy thursday and holy saturday; and on christmas day and the epiphany, when those feasts fall upon sunday or monday ; other- wise, on the days preceding those feasts. also, on st. basil's day, january i; in all, ten times in the course of the year. the liturgy of the presanctified gifts, so called because the holy gifts which have previously been consecrated are used for the holy communion, has existed from ancient times, although, in its present form, it is ascribed to st. gregory homiliastes of rome (sixth century). the orthodox church de- crees that this liturgy shall be celebrated during the great fast (but at no other time), since the triumphantly joyous feelings associated with the corn- plete liturgy and the consecration of the holy gifts are incompatible with the strictness of the fast. hence it is ordained that the complete liturgy shall be celebrated only on saturdays and sundays during the weeks of the great fast (lent). the customary days for the celebration of the liturgy of the presanctified gifts are wednesday and friday of every week, and on monday, tuesday and wednesday of passion week. the liturgy of the presanctified gifts consists of vespers (and therefore is the divine liturgy 65 appointed for a late hour in the day), and of a portion of the ordinary liturgy, omitting the most essential part of the latter, namely, the consecration of the gifts. the liturgy of the presanctified gifts is usually preceded by the read- ing of the third, sixth and ninth hours, and of the typical psalms. under certain circumstances an earlier celebration is admissible. the usual hour for celebrating the ordinary liturgy is, not earlier than dawn, and wt later than noon. for the celebration of the mystery of the eucharist the following are indis- pensable : a priest or a bishop regularly ordained, and having a steadfast will and intention to fulfil the mystery of the lord's body and blood. of material things : five altar-breads, made of pure wheaten flour, and leavened ; wine of the grape. the accomplishment of the mystery through prayer and words, with the blessing of the priest's hand: "and make this bread the precious body of thy christ, and also that which is in this cup the precious blood of thy christ, transmuting them by thy holy spirit." in addition to the above, the following things are indispensable for the liturgy : a corporal (antimfm),* consecrated by a bishop ; vestments for the priest, consisting of a cassock (stikhdr), a stole (cpitrarhfi), gauntlets (p6m/chz], girdle (pbynr), and chasuble w16n) ; vessels, -a chalice, a paten, a star-cover, a spear, a spoon ; veils, a censer, a service book ; lights burning on the altar ; and an acolyte. only one liturgy may be celebrated on any altar in the course of one day ; and no bishop or priest may celebrate more than one liturgy in the course of one and the same day. the priest who enters upon the celebration of the liturgy must be free from inhibition, and from mortal sin, and must prepare himself,- spiritually, , by reconciling himself with all men, by penitence, and the appointed devo- tions ; bodily, by abstinence from food and drink(from midnight at the least), and from fleshly desires, and'by cleanliness of body and garments. the appointed devotions consist of the celebration or the hearing of the evening and morning services and prayers ; and there must also be read : . on monday: the canon to the lord jesus, the invocation to the birthgiver of god, the canon to the archangels; and, if he so desire, to his guardian angel. on tuesday: the canon to the lord jesus, the invocation to the birth-giver of god, to john the forerunner, and to his guardian angel. on wednesday: the canon to the lord jesus, the canon to the birth-giver of god, and to his guardian angel. on thursday: the canon to the lord jesus, the invocation to the birth-giver of god, to his guardian angel, to the holy apostles ; text.en: We speak wisdom, however, among those who are full grown, yet a wisdom not of this world nor of the rulers of this world who are coming to nothing.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:7

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:7

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:7

text.en: But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that has been hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds for our glory,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:8

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:8

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:8

text.en: which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had they known it, they wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 2:9

text.en: But as it is written, “Things which an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him.”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:9

text.en: For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:10

text.en: According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each man be careful how he builds on it.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:11

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:11

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:11

text.en: For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:12

text.en: But if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or straw,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:13

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:13

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:13

text.en: each man’s work will be revealed. For the Day will declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each man’s work is.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:14

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:14

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:14

text.en: If any man’s work remains which he built on it, he will receive a reward.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:15

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:15

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:15

text.en: If any man’s work is burned, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, but as through fire.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:16

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:16

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:16

text.en: Don’t you know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit lives in you?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:17

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:17

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 3:17

text.en: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, which you are.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:1

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:1

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:1

text.en: So let a man think of us as Christ’s servants and stewards of God’s mysteries.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:2

text.en: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:3

text.en: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by a human court. Yes, I don’t even judge my own self.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:4

text.en: For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified by this, but he who judges me is the Lord.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:5

text.en: Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:9

text.en: For I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death. For we are made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:10

text.en: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You have honor, but we have dishonor.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:11

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:11

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:11

text.en: Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:12

text.en: We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:13

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:13

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:13

text.en: Being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:14

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:14

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:14

text.en: I don’t write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:15

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:15

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:15

text.en: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:16

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:16

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:16

text.en: I beg you therefore, be imitators of me.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:17

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:17

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:17

text.en: Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every assembly.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:18

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:18

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:18

text.en: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:19

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:19

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:19

text.en: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing. And I will know, not the word of those who are puffed up, but the power.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:20

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:20

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:20

text.en: For God’s Kingdom is not in word, but in power.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:21

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:21

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 4:21

text.en: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:1

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:1

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:1

text.en: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the Gentiles, that one has his father’s wife.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:2

text.en: You are arrogant, and didn’t mourn instead, that he who had done this deed might be removed from among you.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:3

text.en: For I most certainly, as being absent in body but present in spirit, have already, as though I were present, judged him who has done this thing.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:4

text.en: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together with my spirit with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 5:5

text.en: you are to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:2

text.en: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:3

text.en: My defense to those who examine me is this:

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:4

text.en: Have we no right to eat and to drink?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:5

text.en: Have we no right to take along a wife who is a believer, even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:6

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:6

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:6

text.en: Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:7

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:7

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:7

text.en: What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and doesn’t eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and doesn’t drink from the flock’s milk?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:8

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:8

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:8

text.en: Do I speak these things according to the ways of men? Or doesn’t the law also say the same thing?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:9

text.en: For it is written in the law of Moses, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.” Is it for the oxen that God cares,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:10

text.en: or does he say it assuredly for our sake? Yes, it was written for our sake, because he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes in hope should partake of his hope.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:11

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:11

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:11

text.en: If we sowed to you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap your fleshly things?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 9:12

text.en: If others partake of this right over you, don’t we yet more? Nevertheless we didn’t use this right, but we bear all things, that we may cause no hindrance to the Good News of Christ.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:23

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:23

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:23

text.en: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are profitable. “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:24

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:24

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:24

text.en: Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:25

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:25

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:25

text.en: Whatever is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:26

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:26

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:26

text.en: for “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:27

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:27

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:27

text.en: But if one of those who don’t believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:28

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:28

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 10:28

text.en: But if anyone says to you, “This was offered to idols,” don’t eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience. For “the earth is the Lord’s, with all its fullness.”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:12

text.en: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:13

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:13

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:13

text.en: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:14

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:14

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:14

text.en: For the body is not one member, but many.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:15

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:15

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:15

text.en: If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it is not therefore not part of the body.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:16

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:16

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:16

text.en: If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not therefore not part of the body.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:17

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:17

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:17

text.en: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:18

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:18

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:18

text.en: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:19

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:19

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:19

text.en: If they were all one member, where would the body be?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:20

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:20

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:20

text.en: But now they are many members, but one body.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:21

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:21

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:21

text.en: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:22

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:22

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:22

text.en: No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:23

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:23

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:23

text.en: Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:24

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:24

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:24

text.en: while our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:25

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:25

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:25

text.en: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:26

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:26

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 12:26

text.en: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:4

text.en: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:5

text.en: doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:6

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:6

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:6

text.en: doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:7

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:7

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:7

text.en: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:8

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:8

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:8

text.en: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:9

text.en: For we know in part and we prophesy in part;

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:10

text.en: but when that which is complete has come, then that which is partial will be done away with.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:11

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:11

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:11

text.en: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:12

text.en: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:13

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:13

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 13:13

text.en: But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:1

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:1

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:1

text.en: Follow after love and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:2

text.en: For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God, for no one understands, but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:3

text.en: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, exhortation, and consolation.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:4

text.en: He who speaks in another language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the assembly.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:5

text.en: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but even more that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:6

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:6

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:6

text.en: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:7

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:7

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:7

text.en: Even lifeless things that make a sound, whether pipe or harp, if they didn’t give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known what is piped or harped?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:8

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:8

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:8

text.en: For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:9

text.en: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:10

text.en: There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:11

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:11

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:11

text.en: If then I don’t know the meaning of the language, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and he who speaks would be a foreigner to me.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:12

text.en: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the assembly.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:13

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:13

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:13

text.en: Therefore let him who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:14

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:14

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:14

text.en: For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:15

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:15

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:15

text.en: What should I do? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:16

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:16

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:16

text.en: Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at your giving of thanks, seeing he doesn’t know what you say?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:17

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:17

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:17

text.en: For you most certainly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:18

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:18

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:18

text.en: I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:19

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:19

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:19

text.en: However, in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:26

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:26

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:26

text.en: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, or has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:27

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:27

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:27

text.en: If any man speaks in another language, let there be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:28

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:28

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:28

text.en: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself and to God.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:29

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:29

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:29

text.en: Let two or three of the prophets speak, and let the others discern.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:30

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:30

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:30

text.en: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:31

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:31

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:31

text.en: For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be exhorted.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:32

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:32

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:32

text.en: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:33

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:33

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:33

text.en: for God is not a God of confusion but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:34

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:34

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:34

text.en: Let the wives be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for them to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:35

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:35

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:35

text.en: if they desire to learn anything. “Let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a wife to be talking in the assembly.”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:36

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:36

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:36

text.en: What!? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:37

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:37

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:37

text.en: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:38

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:38

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:38

text.en: But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:39

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:39

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:39

text.en: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and don’t forbid speaking with other languages.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:40

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:40

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 14:40

text.en: Let all things be done decently and in order.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:1

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:1

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:1

text.en: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:2

text.en: by which also you are saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:3

text.en: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:4

text.en: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:5

text.en: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:6

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:6

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:6

text.en: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:7

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:7

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:7

text.en: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:8

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:8

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:8

text.en: and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:9

text.en: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:10

text.en: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:11

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:11

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:11

text.en: Whether then it is I or they, so we preach, and so you believed.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:12

text.en: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:13

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:13

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:13

text.en: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:14

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:14

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:14

text.en: If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith also is in vain.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:15

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:15

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:15

text.en: Yes, we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up if it is true that the dead are not raised.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:16

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:16

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:16

text.en: For if the dead aren’t raised, neither has Christ been raised.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:17

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:17

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:17

text.en: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:18

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:18

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:18

text.en: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:19

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:19

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:19

text.en: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:29

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:29

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:29

text.en: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:30

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:30

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:30

text.en: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:31

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:31

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:31

text.en: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:32

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:32

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:32

text.en: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:33

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:33

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:33

text.en: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:34

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:34

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:34

text.en: Wake up righteously and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:35

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:35

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:35

text.en: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:36

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:36

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:36

text.en: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:37

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:37

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:37

text.en: That which you sow, you don’t sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:38

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:38

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:38

text.en: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:58

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:58

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 15:58

text.en: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:1

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:1

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:1

text.en: Now concerning the collection for the saints: as I commanded the assemblies of Galatia, you do likewise.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:2

text.en: On the first day of every week, let each one of you save as he may prosper, that no collections are made when I come.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:3

text.en: When I arrive, I will send whoever you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:4

text.en: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:5

text.en: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:6

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:6

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:6

text.en: But with you it may be that I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:7

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:7

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:7

text.en: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:8

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:8

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:8

text.en: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:9

text.en: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:10

text.en: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:11

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:11

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:11

text.en: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:12

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:12

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:12

text.en: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:13

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:13

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:13

text.en: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:14

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:14

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:14

text.en: Let all that you do be done in love.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:15

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:15

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:15

text.en: Now I beg you, brothers—you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to serve the saints—

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:16

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:16

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:16

text.en: that you also be in subjection to such, and to everyone who helps in the work and labors.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:17

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:17

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:17

text.en: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on your part, they supplied.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:18

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:18

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:18

text.en: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge those who are like that.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:19

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:19

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:19

text.en: The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the assembly that is in their house.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:20

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:20

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:20

text.en: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:21

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:21

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:21

text.en: This greeting is by me, Paul, with my own hand.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:22

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:22

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:22

text.en: If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be cursed. Come, Lord!

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:23

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:23

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:23

text.en: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:24

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:24

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians 16:24

text.en: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:12

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:12

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:12

text.en: No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:13

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:13

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:13

text.en: By this we know that we remain in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:14

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:14

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:14

text.en: We have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as the Savior of the world.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:15

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:15

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:15

text.en: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:16

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:16

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:16

text.en: We know and have believed the love which God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:17

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:17

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:17

text.en: In this, love has been made perfect among us, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment, because as he is, even so we are in this world.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:18

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:18

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:18

text.en: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.

title.en: John’s First Letter 4:19

summary.en: John’s First Letter 4:19

speaker.en: John’s First Letter 4:19

text.en: We love him, because he first loved us.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:1

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:1

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:1

text.en: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:2

text.en: We always give thanks to God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:3

text.en: remembering without ceasing your work of faith and labor of love and perseverance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:4

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:4

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:4

text.en: We know, brothers loved by God, that you are chosen,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:5

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:5

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:5

text.en: and that our Good News came to you not in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit and with much assurance. You know what kind of men we showed ourselves to be among you for your sake.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:6

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:6

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:6

text.en: You became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:7

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:7

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:7

text.en: so that you became an example to all who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:8

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:8

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:8

text.en: For from you the word of the Lord has been declared, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith toward God has gone out, so that we need not say anything.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:9

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:9

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:9

text.en: For they themselves report concerning us what kind of a reception we had from you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve a living and true God,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:10

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:10

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 1:10

text.en: and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead: Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath to come.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:1

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:1

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:1

text.en: For you yourselves know, brothers, our visit to you wasn’t in vain,

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:2

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:2

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:2

text.en: but having suffered before and been shamefully treated, as you know, at Philippi, we grew bold in our God to tell you the Good News of God in much conflict.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:3

summary.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:3

speaker.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:3

text.en: For our exhortation is not of error, nor of uncleanness, nor in deception.

title.en: Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:4
